fikir: Profesyonel bir tarih filmi sahnesi, 60 saniye: Fausto Zonaro'nun 'Fatih'in İstanbul'a Girişi' tablosunun canlı hâli. Fethin üçüncü günü, Haziran 1453, ikindi. Topkapı'nın şehir içinden görülen büyük kemeri: kireç taşı ve kırmızı tuğla bantlı, hasarlı, kemerin iç yüzünde solmuş bir Bizans freskosu. Güneş kemerin arkasında; kemerin içinden göz alan altın bir ışık ve pus giriyor. Kemerden şehre doğru taş döşeli geniş bir yol; iki yanında omuz omuza yeniçeri kordonu, yalnızca tek beyaz hilalli, yıldızsız, yazısız kırmızı ve yeşil sancaklar; kordonun arkasında, yıkık duvarlarda, damlarda ve pencerelerde binlerce Rum padişahı bekliyor; aralarında altı yaşındaki oğlunu kucağında tutan genç bir anne. Önce sessiz bekleyiş, surların ötesinden ağır mehter. Tören alayı kemerden giriyor: mehter takımı, atlı çavuşlar, sancaktarlar ve yaldızlı alem; sonra tablodaki an: kemerin gölgesinden ışığa, beyaz atının üstünde genç Sultan II. Mehmed (21 yaşında, ince bıyıklı, kısa sakallı, gümüş zırh, kırmızı kaftan, beyaz sorguçlu miğfer) kameraya doğru çıkıyor; sağ eli hafifçe kalkık; solunda önde yaya, ak sakallı, lacivert cübbeli hocası Akşemseddin; arkasında kemerin içini dolduran mızrak ve sancak ormanı, parlak gökyüzüne karşı; ön planda solda kırmızı-altın sarıklı bir muhafız. Alay geçerken kalabalık dalga dalga diz çöküyor; alay kemerin önündeki meydanda duruyor, mehter susuyor, ağır bir sessizlik. Akşemseddin: "Hünkârım, Peygamber efendimizin müjdesi bugün gerçek oldu." Sultan: "Bu zafer bizim değil, Allah'ındır." Sultan diz çökmüş binlerce kişiye bakıyor; anne oğlunu sıkıca tutuyor. Sultan yüksek, sakin ve güven veren bir sesle: "Kalkınız ve müsterih olunuz. Ben Sultan Mehmed; hepinize söylüyorum ki bu andan itibaren ne hürriyetleriniz ne de hayatlarınız hakkında korkmayınız." Binlerce kişi yavaşça ayağa kalkıyor; yüksekten, kemer ve bütün meydan. Kan, ceset, yaralı ya da yağma yok; ağırbaşlı, törensel ve gerçekçi.

mekan.tarif: The inner, city-side face of Topkapı, the great gate in the land walls of Constantinople, seen from inside the city at standing eye level about forty metres away, looking straight west into the gate. The massive round arch of pale limestone with bands of red brick fills the upper middle of the frame; its stones are cracked and scarred by cannon fire, and on the plastered inner face of the arch a large faded Byzantine fresco of a haloed figure in ochre and blue is half flaked away. Through the deep, shadowed passage of the arch the open sky beyond blazes white-gold. From the arch toward the camera runs a broad road of worn stone paving that opens into a wide square. A continuous cordon of janissaries in crimson kaftans and tall white felt börk caps stands shoulder to shoulder along both sides of the road, facing inward, holding tall plain crimson and green banners that each bear only a single white crescent. Behind the cordon, on heaps of fallen masonry, on the wall-walk above the gate, on the flat roofs and in the windows of the stone houses on both sides, thousands of townspeople stand packed and waiting: Greek men, women, old people, children on shoulders, in plain wool clothes of muted earth tones. The stone-paved centre of the road and the square is empty.

The sun stands low in the west directly behind the gate: hazy golden light and drifting dust pour through the arch toward the camera, the passage under the arch is in deep shade, the crowd and the houses are in soft warm shade, and every figure on the road is rim-lit from behind.

bloklar.ozet: High wide shot of the gate and the square packed with thousands waiting in silence; distant mehter beyond the walls. Then at eye level among the crowd: tense faces, the young mother with her son on her hip; the first banners and the mehter emerge from the blazing arch.

Zonaro's painting comes alive: out of the shadow of the arch into the light, the Sultan rides toward the camera on his white horse, Akşemseddin walking ahead at left, a forest of spears and banners behind against the bright sky. The crowd kneels in a wave as he passes; the procession halts; silence.

In the silent square before the gate, Akşemseddin looks up and speaks; the Sultan answers calmly. Close on the kneeling young mother pressing her son to her chest. The Sultan looks over the kneeling thousands.

detailed_description:
The target video is a live-action historical feature film shot on 35mm film with anamorphic lenses, lit only by natural late-afternoon sun, with real crowds of extras. Late afternoon, June 1453. The sun stands low in the west directly behind the gate: hazy golden light and drifting dust pour through the arch toward the camera, the passage under the arch is in deep shade, the crowd and the houses are in soft warm shade, and every figure on the road is rim-lit from behind. Colour palette: crimson red, emerald green, warm limestone cream, terracotta brick, faded fresco ochre and blue, earth-brown and grey wool, burnished silver, white-gold sky. No readable text, calligraphy, signboards, logos or lettering anywhere in the frame, including on the gate, the walls and the houses; the banners carry only a single plain white crescent, with no star and no writing.
[Shot 1] A high wide shot from a flat rooftop inside the city, 24mm lens, looking straight down the axis of the road toward the gate of <Subject 4>. The camera pedestals down with large amplitude at slow speed from above the roofline. The great limestone-and-brick arch fills the upper middle of the frame, its passage in deep shade and the sky beyond blazing white-gold; dust drifts in the light pouring through it. The stone-paved road and the wide square below are empty. Along both sides stands the crimson janissary cordon with its crimson and green single-crescent banners, and behind it thousands of townspeople are packed on heaps of fallen masonry, on the wall-walk above the gate, on flat roofs and in windows; fathers hold children on their shoulders. Nobody moves; only the banners stir in the wind.
[Shot 2] At 00:07.000, the shot cuts to a static eye-level medium shot inside the crowd behind the cordon, 50mm lens, shallow depth of field. In the foreground <Subject 3> stands among tense, silent townspeople, her son on her hip, his face turned into her shoulder; an old man beside her grips his cap with both hands; the red backs and white caps of the janissaries are just in front of them. Far behind, out of focus, the arch blazes with light, and the first tall banners and the mehter band step out of its shadowed passage into the square in strict order. <Subject 3> lifts her eyes toward the gate and holds her breath. From 00:14.000 everyone holds completely still until the end of the shot.

overall_soundscape:
A slow, heavy mehter march of kettle drums, big drums, zurnas and cymbals, muffled beyond the walls at first, then echoing loudly through the arch; the vast, uneasy murmur of thousands of people, wind in the banners, and close whispers hushed at street level.
